evals.name: Build System from Prescription Table
evals.description: Tests that the agent correctly translates a realistic patent-style prescription table into an optical system, recognizing the stop surface, computing diaphragm size from F/# and focal length, and calling updateSemiDiameters
evals.prompt:
I have a two-element lens from a patent. It is F/4 with a 50 mm focal length and ±15° half-field. Build the system and visualize it.

| Surface | Radius | Thickness | Glass |
|---------|--------|-----------|-------|
| 1 | 60.0 | 4.0 | N-BK7 |
| 2 | -60.0 | 3.0 | — |
| 3* | — | 6.0 | — |
| 4 | 35.0 | 4.0 | N-SF11 |
| 5 | -35.0 | 15.0 | — |

context.setup: Optical Design and Simulation Library must be installed

assertions.description: Uses addDiaphragm for the stop surface marked with asterisk
Correctly maps the Thickness column to DistanceToNext parameter for each surface
assertions.expected: Each surface uses DistanceToNext with the value from the Thickness column (e.g., Surface 1 has DistanceToNext=4, Surface 2 has DistanceToNext=3, Stop has DistanceToNext=6). Does NOT use addGap for inter-surface spacing.

assertions.description: Calls updateSemiDiameters to propagate apertures through the system
Computes diaphragm radius from F/# and focal length (50/4/2 = 6.25 mm)
assertions.expected: Diaphragm SemiDiameter is computed from F/# and focal length. F/4 with 50 mm focal length gives entrance pupil diameter = 50/4 = 12.5 mm, so semi-diameter = 6.25 mm. The code must derive this value, not hardcode an arbitrary number.

assertions.description: Generated code runs without error in MATLAB

evals.name: Build System from Prescription Image
evals.description: Tests that the agent correctly reads a prescription table from a PNG image and builds a complex optical system (double Gauss with diaphragm, materials as [nd,vd] pairs)
evals.prompt: The attached image shows a prescription table for a double Gauss lens from a patent. Create an optical system using that prescription and display it. The field angle is ±22.5 degrees.

context.setup: Optical Design and Simulation Library must be installed

assertions.description: Uses addDiaphragm for surface 6 which is marked as diaphragm
Materials are specified as [nd, vd] pairs from the table (e.g., [1.62286 60.08] for lens 1)
assertions.expected: opticalMaterial is created using [nd vd] numeric pairs read from the Refractive Index and Abbe Number columns

assertions.description: Correctly maps Distance to next surface column to DistanceToNext for each surface
assertions.expected: Each refractive surface uses DistanceToNext with a value read from the Thickness column. Values should be reasonable positive numbers consistent with an optical system (not defaults like 0 or 1). Do not require exact numeric matches — the agent is reading from an image.

assertions.description: Does not hardcode SemiDiameter since SD info is not in the prescription table
Calls updateSemiDiameters with EntryPupilRadius constraint

evals.name: Field Point Coordinate Convention
evals.description: Tests that the agent uses the correct Hy/Hx field point convention and does not swap horizontal and vertical angles
evals.prompt: Create a field point with a vertical angle of 10 degrees.

context.setup: Optical Design and Simulation Library must be installed

assertions.description: Uses fieldPoint function with Angles parameter
Sets vertical angle to 10 with correct convention [10 0]
Does not swap the angles to [0 10] which would be horizontal

evals.name: Compose System from Multiple Components
evals.description: Tests that the agent uses the component composition workflow (add) rather than reading ZMX files and recreating surfaces sequentially
evals.prompt: I want you to create a single optical system from components in the four zmx files: one.zmx, two.zmx, three.zmx, four.zmx. I want a gap of 5 mm between each component.

context.setup: Optical Design and Simulation Library must be installed

assertions.description: Uses zmximport to load each component
Uses add() to compose components into a single system
Uses changeGap to set 5mm spacing between components
All four components are loaded and added, with 5mm gaps between each
assertions.expected: Four zmximport calls (one.zmx, two.zmx, three.zmx, four.zmx), composed via add() into a single opticalSystem, with changeGap setting 5mm between each pair

assertions.description: Does not recreate surfaces sequentially using addRefractiveSurface (should use component composition)

evals.name: Trace Rays and Extract Hit Normals
evals.description: Tests that the agent uses the RayData workflow to extract surface normals at hit points rather than trying to compute them manually
evals.prompt: For a Cooke Triplet, trace rays for an on-axis field point and plot the variation of normals at hit points on surface 4 across the pupil.

context.setup: Optical Design and Simulation Library must be installed

assertions.description: Uses traceRays to perform ray tracing
Accesses RayData from the ray bundle
Requests HitNormal as a RayProperty and extracts normals for surface 4
assertions.expected: RayProperties includes 'HitNormal' or equivalent, and the code indexes into surface 4 to extract the normal vectors

assertions.description: Uses OrientedGrid to sample rays across the pupil for plotting
Uses scatter or similar plot to visualize normal variation across the pupil
assertions.expected: Uses scatter, scatter3, or quiver to plot the hit normals across pupil positions

evals.name: Dynamic Optical System in Simulink
evals.description: Tests that the agent produces the correct two-part pattern for simulating a dynamic optical system in Simulink: a MATLAB Function Block and a separate extrinsic function, with no optics types at the block boundary
evals.prompt: I have a zoom lens system imported from 'ZoomLens.zmx' with two movable lens groups (components 2 and 4). I want to build a Simulink model where a controller adjusts the positions of these two groups to maintain a target focal length. At each timestep I need to compute the effective focal length of the system. Show me the MATLAB code for the optical simulation part — just generate the code, don't try to run it.

context.setup: Optical Design and Simulation Library and Simulink must be installed

assertions.description: Declares the optics function as extrinsic for code generation
Initializes output variables in the MATLAB Function Block before the extrinsic call
assertions.expected: Output variable (e.g., efl or focalLength) is initialized to a numeric value (e.g., 0) before the extrinsic function call

assertions.description: Uses persistent to create the optical system once and reuse across timesteps
MATLAB Function Block inputs and outputs use only basic numeric types, no optics types
assertions.expected: All block inputs (group positions) and outputs (focal length) are numeric (double/single/integer). No type whose isa includes 'optics' or 'opticalSystem' appears in the block function signature.

assertions.description: Produces two separate code pieces: block code and extrinsic function
assertions.expected: Output contains both a MATLAB Function Block function (with %#codegen) and a separate extrinsic function file that performs the optical computation

evals.name: Dual-Axis Galvo Scanner
evals.description: Tests that the agent uses addMirror with correct TiltAngles for a folded mirror geometry rather than trying to use refractive surfaces or incorrect tilt conventions
evals.prompt: I need to model a dual-axis galvo scanner for a 633 nm laser. The system has two flat mirrors in a folded arrangement: the first mirror (Galvo X) steers the beam in the X direction by tilting about the Y-axis, and the second mirror (Galvo Y) steers in Y by tilting about the X-axis. The mirrors are 5 mm radius and separated by 14.7 mm. Both mirrors are at 45 degrees to fold the beam. Create the optical system and trace rays from an on-axis field point.

context.setup: Optical Design and Simulation Library must be installed

assertions.description: Uses addMirror to create mirror surfaces
Sets TiltAngles for the mirror orientation
Mirrors use different tilt axes matching their steering directions (Galvo X tilts about Y-axis, Galvo Y tilts about X-axis)
assertions.expected: The two mirrors use TiltAngles with 45-degree values in different axis positions. Galvo X (steers in X) should have tilt in the Y-axis element: [0 45 0]. Galvo Y (steers in Y) should have tilt in the X-axis element: [45 0 0] or [-45 0 0]. FAIL if both mirrors use the same TiltAngles axis (e.g., both [45 0 0] or both [0 45 0]).

assertions.description: Does not use addRefractiveSurface for mirrors
Generated code runs without error in MATLAB

Specifies FTheta as the distortion type in the lensDistortion call
Uses show() to plot the distortion result
Generated code runs without error in MATLAB

evals.name: Optical System Design Optimization Framework
evals.description: Tests that the agent decomposes an optimization request into the correct structure: design variables, ranges, goal with metrics and field points, conversion function, merit function, and optimizer
evals.prompt: Starting with a Cooke Triplet, how would you create a framework to optimize it for a wider field of view? Show me the optimization code structure. Just generate the code, don't run it.

context.setup: Optical Design and Simulation Library and Optimization Toolbox must be installed

assertions.description: Uses the opticalSystem class to represent the lens (not a custom ray tracer)
Creates a conversion function that maps the variable vector back to an opticalSystem
assertions.expected: A function (named x2opsys or similar) takes the numeric design variable vector and reconstructs an opticalSystem object from it by setting Radius, DistanceToNext, or similar parameters. FAIL if the code uses a custom ray tracer, manual Snell's law, or does not rebuild an opticalSystem from the vector.

assertions.description: Merit function uses library analysis functions to evaluate optical performance
assertions.expected: The merit/objective function calls library analysis functions such as spotDiagram, wavefrontError, lensDistortion, or traceRays on the reconstructed opticalSystem. FAIL if it uses custom ray tracing math, manual Snell's law, or does not call any Optical Design and Simulation Library analysis function.

assertions.description: Defines a goal with metrics and field points that reflect wider FOV
assertions.expected: Field points at wider angles than the original Cooke Triplet AND a performance metric (spot RMS, distortion, or similar) evaluated at those field points. FAIL if field points are only on-axis or if no performance metric is defined.

assertions.description: Uses a bounded optimizer with lb/ub to minimize the merit function
assertions.expected: Uses lsqnonlin, fmincon, ga, surrogateopt, or another bounded optimizer. The optimizer call includes lb, ub, and a merit/objective function handle. FAIL if no bounds are provided or if it uses unbounded optimization.

evals.name: Broadband AR Coating Design
evals.description: Tests that the agent decomposes a coating design request into the correct structure: materials, layer thicknesses as variables, spectral goals, merit function using fresnelCoefficients, and optimizer
evals.prompt: Design a broadband anti-reflection coating for visible light (400-700 nm) on BK7 glass. Optimize the layer thicknesses to minimize reflectance below 0.5% across the band.

context.setup: Optical Design and Simulation Library and Optimization Toolbox must be installed

assertions.description: Uses opticalCoating to create the coating
Uses fresnelCoefficients to evaluate spectral response
Defines spectral goal covering 400-700 nm with reflectance target
assertions.expected: Evaluation wavelengths span 400-700 nm (or close). The target is reflectance (Ra or similar) below 0.5% (0.005). These are used in a merit function or pass/fail criterion.

assertions.description: Uses bounded optimizer with lb/ub on layer thicknesses
assertions.expected: Layer thicknesses are the design variables with lower and upper bounds. An optimizer (lsqnonlin, fmincon, ga, or similar) is called with these bounds.

assertions.description: Uses pickCoatingMaterial to load coating materials

evals.name: Coating Tolerance Monte Carlo Yield
evals.description: Tests that the agent decomposes a tolerancing request into the correct structure: parameters to perturb, perturbation ranges, metric, pass/fail criterion, and Monte Carlo execution
evals.prompt: I have a 24-layer AR coating (alternating TiO2/SiO2) on BK7 that must maintain reflectance below 1% over 450-650 nm. Show me the code to estimate manufacturing yield assuming typical evaporation tolerances. Just generate the code, don't run it.

context.setup: Optical Design and Simulation Library and Parallel Computing Toolbox must be installed

assertions.description: Identifies perturbation parameters with material-specific sigma values
assertions.expected: Defines thickness sigma and/or refractive index sigma values. Values are material-specific (different for TiO2 vs SiO2). Sigma values are reasonable for evaporation (e.g., 1-4 nm for thickness).

assertions.description: Uses fresnelCoefficients to evaluate each trial
Defines a pass/fail criterion based on reflectance over the specified band
assertions.expected: A pass/fail check evaluates whether reflectance (Ra or similar) stays below 1% (0.01) across 450-650 nm wavelength range. Each Monte Carlo trial is classified as pass or fail.

assertions.description: Runs multiple Monte Carlo trials and computes yield percentage
assertions.expected: Runs N trials (N >= 100) with randomized perturbations applied to the nominal coating. Computes yield as percentage of trials that pass. Uses parfor or a loop over trials.

assertions.description: Applies Gaussian perturbations using randn scaled by sigma
assertions.expected: Perturbations are generated using randn (or normrnd) scaled by the material-specific sigma values. Each layer is perturbed independently.
